D. Different Site Design Philosophy
Consideration was also given to limiting demonstrations on a given site to one housing system, and permitting this system to demonstrate many different types of housing. However, the number of good housing systems obtained through the competition and evaluation, together with budget limitations and marketing objectives, required that all systems be permitted as wide an exposure as possible. Final site designs and housing system mixes have been based on budgetary, site design and system marketing area considerations.
5. RELATIONSHIP EETWEEN LOCAL SHORT-TERM USES OF MAN'S ENVIRONMENT AND THE MAINTENANCE OF AN ENHANCEMENT OF LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY
Operation BREAKTHROUGH, as a program, is directed to improving the supply and quality of housing. From the perspective that each generation is a trustee of the environment for succeeding generations, the success of PREAKTHROUGH in meeting its objectives will have beneficial long term effects.
Each of the prototype sites involve changes in existing land usage. Four of the sites initiate development of land stripped for urban renewal, two utilize land retired from previous uses, and three require development of housing on land which formerly was open and unused. In each case, the site planning and development program, as described in the foregoing material, has been directed to the development of an attractive, viable community with long-term housing potential. Care has been taken to retain those features which will enhance the environment of the individual sites. It is felt that the BREAKTHROUGH sites represent developmental approaches appropriate to good long-term utilization of this land.
6. IRREVERSIBLE AND IRFETRIEVABLE COMMITMENTS OF RESOURCES
To the extent that resources of materials, labor and money are expended in the physical development of the BREAKTHROUGH sites, these are irreversible. Physically, it will be possible to remove BREAKTHROUGH construction should this ever become desirable, but the probability of this happening is extremely low.
From a program point of view, much of the effort in developing new housing technology is directed to a better utilization of resources in housing construction, and particularly to finding alternatives to resources in limited supply.
7. COMMENTS ON DRAFT ENVIRONMENTAL STATEMENT BY OTHER FEDERAL AGENCIES WITH HUD RESPONSES
Where appropriate, comments have been addressed in the text of the Final Statement rather than receiving specific responses below. In such cases, the phrase, "See Final Statement" has been used as a response.
